# Prepare Release Skill

How a release of **Historic City Map Maker** is prepared. Releases are git tags `vX.Y.Z` (or pre-releases `vX.Y.Z-beta.N` / `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) on `master`; the engine is served to other cities from this repository's tags through jsDelivr: the release commit carries the built engine in `cdn/engine/` with `cdn/engine/release.json` (the version, the pinned folder, the SHA-384 integrity of every file), which jsDelivr serves at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-city-map-maker@vX.Y.Z/cdn/engine/` (an exact version, pinned with SRI by the starter kit) and at `@1` (the major line, never with SRI). Bucharest serves the engine of its own commit same-origin from GitHub Pages. The contract is `docs/research/M5-interfaces.md` §2; the first release is the pre-release **v1.0.0-beta.1**, prepared and never tagged without the user.

## Procedure

1. **Version.** Pick `X.Y.Z` by semantic versioning of the engine's public surface (`docs/ENGINE_API.md` → *Versioning and compatibility*: the `HistoricCityMap` global and the module build's exports, `<hcm-map-viewer>` and its events, `config.js`, the URL hash, the City Manifest). The tag must match `^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-(beta|rc)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?$`: a release, or a pre-release `-beta.N` / `-rc.N` (N without leading zeros), no other suffix. A pre-release: the GitHub Release is a pre-release and never marked latest (`release.yml` reads the tag); it is pinned on jsDelivr only at its full version (`@v1.0.0-beta.1`; the notes offer no `@1` line, and no `@1` purge runs for it); an npm publish uses its channel as dist-tag (`npm publish … --tag beta`, `releaseDistTag` of `@hcm/shared`), never `latest`; `compareVersions` orders `1.0.0-beta.1` < `1.0.0-rc.1` < `1.0.0`, so a manifest needing `1.0.0` refuses a beta engine.
2. **Bump, in the image:** `npm run release:bump -- X.Y.Z` (`scripts/release/bump.ts`). It rewrites, and only rewrites, the version of the root `package.json`, every workspace `package.json` (`create-historic-city` among them) and every dependency of a workspace on another workspace, their entries in `package-lock.json`, `functions/deploy-lock/package.json` and its lock (the deploy artifact carries the functions' version, `functions/build.mjs` compares the text), and `ENGINE_VERSION` in `packages/engine/src/index.ts`. Nothing is resolved or downloaded: the pipeline's `npm ci` from the image's offline cache accepts the result, and the image's npm layer stays cached, because its `manifests` stage writes the workspaces' versions as 0.0.0 (`docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §63b; check with `docker build --target manifests` that its output did not change before a build that would miss the cache). The About dialog's spec reads the version from the root `package.json`, so no test changes with it.
3. **The released engine, in the image:** `npm run build --workspace @hcm/engine && npm run release:cdn` (`scripts/release/cdn.ts`) replaces `cdn/engine/` with every file of `packages/engine/dist` but the source maps (each built file's last `//# sourceMappingURL=` line removed, every text file ending in a newline) and writes `release.json` (`engineReleaseSchema`; Mapbox GL JS's integrity from the installed npm release, as the site build computes it; the files in code-point order). Never edit `cdn/engine/` by hand: the `release-cdn` gate rebuilds it and compares byte for byte.
4. **The kit's pins:** `npm run release:pin-kit` rewrites the engine block and the meta CSP of `templates/starter-kit/index.html` from `release.json` through `fillKitPage` (`@hcm/shared`); Mapbox GL JS's tags are the template's own and must already name the release's (a newer Mapbox GL JS is a template change before the release).
   Then `npm run build:landing`: the landing page (`sites/landing/`, GitHub Pages, DECISIONS §162) names `npx create-historic-city@<version>`; the static `landing` gate refuses a stale folder.
5. **Release notes**, two files (`docs/releases/README.md`):
   - `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md`: the full notes (features, fixes, security, breaking changes, migration, verification results).
   - `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z_github_description.md`: the GitHub Release body; its single H1 (`# Release vX.Y.Z - <title>`) becomes the release title. It holds the markers `<!-- hcm:sri -->` and `<!-- /hcm:sri -->`; `npm run release:notes -- --write docs/releases/vX.Y.Z_github_description.md` writes between them the table of pinned addresses with their integrity, the `@1` folder and the four tags to paste. The releases index (*Releases* in `docs/releases/README.md`) gains the version.
6. **Docs drift.** Review the full diff since the previous tag against `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, the admin guide (`docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.en.md`) and the agent assets; update what drifted (`governance/doc_update_skill.md`).
7. **Pipeline, before tagging, in the image:** `python3 scripts/ci/check_release.py --tag vX.Y.Z` (what `release-check` checks on the tag) and, after a fresh `npm run build`, `npm run release:cdn -- --check` (what `release-cdn` checks); `kit-pins` runs in `static`. Then `bash scripts/ci/e2e-split.sh` (the default stage `all`, split with the NUC) must end in `[SUCCESS] stage 'all' passed`. When the NUC's BuildKit cache was evicted (it builds other projects), its first split run rebuilds the quality image from the registries: that is a download, so ask first, or run `bash scripts/ci/run-all-checks.sh` on this machine only (§63g). `PIPELINE_STAGE=release` itself runs in CI on the tag: its `release-check` needs the tag at HEAD.
8. **Ask first**, one action at a time, each command printed for the user (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push` refuses a push to `master` or a tag without the green `all` marker of that commit):
   1. `git push origin feat/engine-rewrite`
   2. the pull request to `master` (`gh pr create --base master --head feat/engine-rewrite`), its review, the merge;
   3. on the merged commit of `master`, after `all` is green there: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z"`
   4. `git push origin vX.Y.Z`

## Where the first release stands (2026-11-12)

- The engine's `engine.css` changed after the committed `cdn/engine/` (2026-11-12, `docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §188b: the kit's viewer a flow root, its page an app shell once the viewer is defined): until step 3 runs again, the tour's `kit.loading-note` fails `no-blank-scroll` (the page scrolls 24 px past its note), since the e2e serves the committed release. Step 3 is the fix; never a hand edit of `cdn/engine/`.
- v1.0.0-beta.1 is prepared on `feat/engine-rewrite` (`docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §160, §161): every version is 1.0.0-beta.1, `cdn/engine/` and the kit's pins name it, both notes files and the index are written, the repository is `ventura8/historic-city-map-maker`. The ask-first steps of step 8 remain.
- 2026-11-13: the beta's tag passes `check_release.py`'s pattern and `release.yml` marks it a pre-release, never latest. The notes gained a *New in the last days* section with `TODO (<track>)` lines for the tracks still landing; at the freeze, delete every TODO line, then run step 3 to 5 again (the committed `cdn/engine/` and the description's pinned block are stale until then, and that chain was proved to end in `[release] OK`).
- §59c needs no answer any more: `npm run release:cdn` writes lit-html's whitespace class with escapes, so the committed engine passes `editorconfig` with no exception. The v1.0.0 notes stay prepared for the release after the betas.

## What CI does on a tag (`release.yml`)

- Job `build` (`contents: read`) runs `PIPELINE_STAGE=release` in the quality image: `release-check` (the tag, every version, `cdn/engine/release.json`, the kit's pinned folder, both notes files and the description's pinned addresses), `kit-pins`, `vite-build`, `release-cdn` (`cdn/engine/` byte for byte a fresh build; the first run on CI proves the build reproducible across machines), `bundle-budget`, `notices`, `hosting-build`, `start-build`, `self-host-bundle` (the CLI's `dist/self-host/` from that production build, its hosting folder the start site's release tree; it refuses the admin's e2e build) and `release-pack` (`create-historic-city-X.Y.Z.tgz` in `reports/release/`, with its self-host bundle). `release-check` also checks that the guides that tell a reader to run the CLI (`PINNED_DOCS`) name the tag's exact version (`npx create-historic-city@X.Y.Z`, never `@1`), which `npm run release:bump` rewrites. It shows the pinned addresses and their integrity in the job summary (`reports/release/engine-addresses.md`) and uploads the bundles and `docs/releases/` as the `release` artifact.
- Job `publish`, the only one with `contents: write`, checks nothing out and runs no repository code: it downloads that artifact and creates the GitHub Release titled by the H1 of the description file (the tag when there is none), with the description file as body and `packages/engine/dist/*` and `packages/admin/dist/*` attached (the source maps among them).
- jsDelivr needs no step: it serves the tag's `cdn/engine/` on the first request and keeps an exact tag's files for good.
- Proposed, waiting for the user (`docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §58c): the SonarQube gate of the same commit, `release.json` and the CLI's package attached to the GitHub Release, and the purge of the `@1` alias (`https://purge.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-city-map-maker@1/cdn/engine/<file>` per file of `release.json`).

## After the tag (the user's steps, ask first)

- The starter kit's template repository (`docs/research/M5-interfaces.md` §3.5): `gh repo create ventura8/historic-city-map-starter --public`, push a copy of `templates/starter-kit/`, `gh api -X PATCH repos/ventura8/historic-city-map-starter -F is_template=true`; every later release pushes the newly pinned `index.html` there.
- `create-historic-city` on npm (§4.6), in the user's own terminal: `npm view create-historic-city`, `npm login`, `npm publish reports/release/create-historic-city-X.Y.Z.tgz --access public`. Claude never types the password or the one-time code. The name is checked and published (or reserved) **before** the merge that makes the guides naming it public: whoever registers it first runs code on every reader of `npx create-historic-city@…` (`docs/LESSONS.md` 238; `docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §65e, which also proposes publishing the CI-packed tarball with `--provenance` from `release.yml`, a workflow edit for the user).

## Rules

- Release notes describe what shipped, verified against the code; no test counts (they live only in `docs/E2E_SCENARIOS.md`).
- A breaking change of the manifest or `config.js` is a major version and documents the migration for city owners.
- jsDelivr limits (150 MB per package, 20 MB per file) are why photos live in Storage, not in the tree at a tag; the `repo-budget` gate (`scripts/ci/check_repo_budget.py`) keeps the tree small, and `cdn/engine/` (about 1 MB) is replaced, never added to, so the tree holds one release at a time.
- The release transform writes lit-html's whitespace class, which the minifier emits as a template literal with a raw tab and line break (a trailing space and tab for `editorconfig`), with escapes: the untagged literal's value is the same string (`docs/research/DECISIONS-for-review.md` §160). A new trailing-whitespace finding in `cdn/engine/` is fixed in that transform, never with an `.editorconfig` exception. Prettier and ESLint ignore the folder (their own ignore files, the pre-approved kind). The suppression scan, gitleaks (both configurations), markdownlint, `data-files`, `repo-policy` and `repo-budget` pass on it as it is.
